about: GHOST ATLAS starter library: where every sound comes from, who made it and under what licence. Fetched by fetch_library.py; nothing here is behind a login.

libraries.name: Glasses of water
libraries.author: FreePats project and its contributors (see credit)
libraries.credit: Simple musical instrument made with glasses of water. It was recorded on October 2019, initially as an example for a workshop in Medialab-Prado. It turned out more interesting than expected and it's now transformed into a sound bank. Recorded with an AKG Perception 120 microphone and glasses of water, carefully filled to tune into chromatic sounds with aproximate note range from A4 to G6.

libraries.name: Caveman Cosmonaut
libraries.author: Karoryfer Samples
libraries.credit: A synthesizer made from samples of a 1983 Unitra B 11 transistor organ: its own program and its thirteen presets (Supersawism, Evolving Pad, Plucky Pluck, Dramatic Bass, E-Piano, Unstable Lead and more).
libraries.note: Its programs open their filter with ARIA-only 'var' modulations, which sfizz does not play (the filter stayed shut and only the low end was heard). fetch_library.py (caveman_cosmonaut) writes the same opening in standard SFZ and makes each of its thirteen ARIA presets an SFZ program; the recordings and mappings are untouched. Each program also gets its own copy of the instrument's maps holding only the regions it can sound (about 12,000 regions for every oscillator type, unison voice and mono mode, chosen by controls a program sets once): a program loads in a tenth of the time, and sounds the same.

libraries.name: Ghost Atlas Synth Renders (Surge XT)
libraries.author: Surge Synth Team (Surge XT and its factory patches); rendered by the Ghost Atlas Preset Factory
libraries.credit: Twenty Surge XT factory patches (trance saws, plucks, pads, an FM electric piano, FM bells, basses) played offline through Surge XT's own engine into multisampled instruments: notes every 3 semitones, one or two velocities, dry, held sounds looped.
libraries.license: Surge XT output: free to use (Surge XT itself is GPL-3.0)
libraries.restrictions: none: the Surge team states that sounds made with Surge XT, factory patches included, may be used, given away or sold
libraries.note: Made once on the Mac (it is already in the Library folder there) and not downloaded: renders.json beside the files says which Surge XT patch each instrument came from.

libraries.name: Ghost Atlas Synth Renders, set 2 (OB-Xd, Dexed, Vaporizer2, Odin 2)
libraries.author: discoDSP (OB-Xd 2), Pascal Gauthier and contributors (Dexed; voices from the Synprez FM banks it ships with), VAST Dynamics (Vaporizer2), TheWaveWarden and contributors (Odin 2); rendered by the Ghost Atlas Preset Factory
libraries.credit: 73 factory patches from four synthesisers played offline into multisampled instruments: notes every 3 semitones (every 4 for pads), one or two velocities, 48 kHz 24-bit FLAC, dry (the synths' own delays, reverbs, choruses and arpeggiators off), held sounds looped with a crossfade. OB 14, DX 15, VZ 23, Odin 21. Made by tools/factory/render_plugins.py; renders.json says which patch each came from.
libraries.license: Rendered output of GPL-3.0 synthesisers (Dexed, Vaporizer2, Odin 2) and of the freeware OB-Xd 2; factory patches by their authors
libraries.restrictions: Private: for Brandon's own Ghost Atlas only, not to be shared or sold. The synths' code licences do not cover their factory patches, and OB-Xd 2's own licence text asks for personal use.
libraries.note: Made once and put on the Mac (it is already in the Library folder there), not downloaded: renders.json beside the files says which patch each instrument came from; tools/factory/specs/ holds the lists it was made from.

libraries.name: Meta Open Sound (piano and guitars)
libraries.author: Meta's Creative Audio team
libraries.credit: A full 88-key upright piano with four velocity layers, a nylon-string guitar and a steel-string guitar, each multisampled string by string.
libraries.note: The 24-bit / 48 kHz WAV recordings from the repository's releases (the largest zip of each). A guitar whose release cannot be had comes from the repository's own OGG Vorbis copies instead; the piano's copies there are Opus, which the engine cannot read, so the piano is always the release. Its game and VR sound effects (CC BY 4.0) are left out.

libraries.note: Only its textures, guitar effects, found sounds and noise: its drums, loops and spoken one-shots are not instruments, and its VCSL and VSCO pieces are already here in full.
